profiles.meeting_scenario: At Meridian Crest Asset Management, a Director of Quant Research and a Product Strategy Manager are holding a planning meeting about whether to move a SARL-inspired reinforcement-learning portfolio strategy from research prototype into an internal pilot for the firm's Technology Opportunities equity sleeve. The strategy augments portfolio state inputs with asset movement predictions derived from market data and Reuters news, and the firm wants to showcase it at the September Innovation Committee as a possible next-generation overlay strategy. The agenda is to align on the pilot setup, required data and platform support, scope of the target asset universe, responsibilities across research/product/compliance, and the timeline for a committee readout. The expected outcome is an apparently shared plan for what will be built over the next eight weeks, who owns each dependency, and what will be presented in September.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Reinforcement learning for trading, portfolio optimization, financial NLP, backtesting methodology
members.background: Priya joined Meridian Crest after leading systematic investing research at a fintech lab and previously publishing academic work on RL-based asset allocation with alternative data.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve momentum from a promising research result and avoid the pilot being slowed down by production-level process requirements before the strategy has shown enough signal quality internally.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means a shadow portfolio that logs daily target weights and performance without sending executable orders into the firm's trading stack.
A 'live data hookup' is satisfied by end-of-day prices and a pre-market batch of processed Reuters news features because the strategy only updates once per day.
The relevant 'HighTech universe' is the cleaned 42-name research universe with continuous price history and consistent Reuters article coverage.
Something is 'ready for committee' once the team has a convincing backtest, a short shadow-track record, and turnover statistics that look commercially plausible.

members.name: Daniel Brooks
members.expertise: Investment product planning, internal launch governance, data vendor coordination, committee materials and operating model definition
members.background: Daniel has spent nine years translating research ideas into internal pilots and approved offerings for multi-asset and thematic equity products at large asset managers.
members.private_state: He wants the September committee discussion to look operationally credible so the strategy can win budget and executive sponsorship, and he worries that a research-only demo will be dismissed as immature.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means the strategy runs through the production-adjacent workflow with pre-trade checks and is close enough to execution that the committee can treat it as launchable if approved.
A 'live data hookup' means integration to the firm's monitored streaming market and news feeds with entitlements, timestamps, and operational failover, even if the model ultimately rebalances daily.
The target 'tech sleeve' is the firm's standard 67-name Tech Innovators universe, reconstituted monthly and used in existing product reporting.
Something is 'ready for committee' only if the materials also show mandate fit, drawdown behavior within product guardrails, and a workable operational/control model.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the pilot being 'live'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about getting the 'pilot' running by mid-August and taking it to the September committee.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means a shadow book producing daily recommended weights and tracked P&L outside the execution stack.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means a production-adjacent pilot that passes pre-trade checks and is operationally executable, even if capital is still limited or internal.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both functions regularly use the word 'pilot' and each treats their version as the standard default, so the term creates easy surface agreement while hiding a materially different level of operational readiness.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the model needs a 'live data hookup' before the pilot starts.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a nightly price refresh plus a pre-market batch of processed Reuters news features delivered to the research environment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means connection to the firm's monitored intraday market/news feed infrastructure with entitlements, production timestamps, and support expectations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The disagreement is not over whether data is needed but over the implied operating cadence and platform standard, which each person sees as an obvious implementation detail rather than something that needs explicit confirmation.

misalignment_points.topic: Which asset set is 'the tech sleeve'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to launching the strategy on the 'HighTech universe' or 'tech sleeve' as if it were a single agreed set of names.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of a fixed 42-stock universe chosen for clean seven-year history and reliable Reuters coverage used in research replication.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the firm's current 67-name Tech Innovators sleeve used in product reporting, including recent additions and monthly reconstitutions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Universe membership feels like background context inherited from each person's normal workflow, so neither expects that the same thematic label could hide a different count, eligibility rule, and reconstitution method.

misalignment_points.topic: What makes the strategy 'ready for committee'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the goal is to have something 'ready for committee' or a 'good September readout.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means persuasive backtest evidence, a short shadow-performance readout, and portfolio behavior that looks reasonable relative to the benchmark.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means those results plus evidence the strategy fits mandate guardrails, has acceptable drawdown behavior for the sleeve, and can be described in an operationally credible launch packet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely aiming for a successful committee discussion, but 'ready' is an evaluative term whose standards come from their own departmental norms, so the mismatch stays latent during otherwise cooperative planning.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep the momentum from the recent result and not let this get dragged into production formalities too early. For me the goal is straightforward: get a shadow portfolio running on the cleaned 42-name HighTech research universe, log daily target weights and P&L for a few weeks, and bring that plus the backtest to the September committee. The SARL-style setup is already compelling because the portfolio state improves when we add the Reuters-derived movement signals.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. From my side, the objective is to get the SARL-based pilot onto the tech sleeve in time for a good September readout. The model itself is in pretty solid shape now: we’re augmenting the portfolio state with predicted asset-movement signals from market data and Reuters news, and that’s been meaningfully helpful versus the earlier baseline.

turns.inner_thought: That timeline is fine if we can show something operationally credible, not just a research demo. I want the committee to see a pilot that is effectively launchable pending approval, which means production-adjacent workflow, controls, and a live data hookup that looks like our normal monitored setup. If it is running by mid-August, I can package it well for September and use that to secure budget.

What I need to understand today is what has to happen around the live data hookup and the governance pieces so we’re supporting that on the right path.

I don't want to imply we need more than that.

turns.inner_thought: Parallel running is fine as long as it still looks like the sleeve could absorb it. If I can show fit and oversight, executives will take it seriously.
turns.utterance: That makes sense to me. For the committee, I’ll also want to show how this fits within the sleeve’s existing limits and monitoring expectations, so the September discussion lands as a serious next step rather than just an interesting research update.

turns.inner_thought: I can absolutely provide what I consider the key evidence: backtest results, turnover, and daily shadow allocations on the 42 names we’ve been using. If that starts in August, we’ll have enough days of tracked recommendations and P&L to support the committee conversation without overcommitting to full production build-out.
